articles.title: 64 Rochdale food businesses rated 0 or 1 for hygiene
articles.excerpt: A total of 64 food businesses in Rochdale hold a food hygiene rating of 0 or 1, indicating urgent or major improvements are necessary, according to the Food Standards Agency.
articles.content_html:
A total of 64 food businesses in the Rochdale borough currently hold a food hygiene rating of 0 or 1, according to records from the Food Standards Agency checked on 29 July 2026. Five businesses are rated 0, where urgent improvement is necessary, while 59 are rated 1, indicating major improvement is necessary.

Among the businesses rated 0 are Yo 1 Stop, a retailer located at 1 Middleton Road, Heywood, which received its rating following an inspection on 22 June 2026. Other businesses rated 0 include Apple & Pears, a pub at Andover Avenue, and Wildbloods of Norden Limited, a retailer on Edenfield Road, both rated 0 after inspections in March 2026. Knockout Diner, a takeaway on Baillie Street, and Frozen Delights and Convenience, a restaurant on the same street, were also rated 0 after inspections in February and December 2025, respectively.

The businesses rated 1 include Davids, a takeaway on Dale Street, and Grillo, a takeaway on Heady Hill Road, both rated 1 after inspections on 30 June 2026. Other establishments with a rating of 1 include Denehurst Stores, Meanwood Stores, and several retailers on Oldham Road, all of which received their ratings in June 2026. Notable mentions also include Zam Zam Kitchen, a takeaway on Milkstone Road, and Marland Court, a caring premises, both rated 1 after inspections in June and May 2026, respectively.

The Food Standards Agency provides these ratings to inform the public about food hygiene standards. Businesses rated 0 or 1 are encouraged to make improvements to ensure compliance with hygiene regulations. The ratings serve as a guide for consumers when choosing where to eat or purchase food.

articles.title: Graffiti Removal Initiative Launched in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A new initiative aims to tackle graffiti in Rochdale, with No Graffiti Ltd leading the effort to clean up public spaces.
articles.content_html:
A new initiative has been launched to address graffiti in Rochdale. No Graffiti Ltd is spearheading the effort to remove unwanted markings from public spaces.

The campaign aims to improve the appearance of the area and enhance community pride. Local residents and businesses are encouraged to report instances of graffiti to facilitate timely removal.

No Graffiti Ltd has extensive experience in graffiti removal and is committed to restoring affected areas. The initiative is expected to contribute positively to the local environment.

Residents can participate by reporting graffiti sightings to the local council or directly to No Graffiti Ltd, helping to keep Rochdale clean and welcoming.

articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has published a document detailing anticipated reasons for potential restrictions affecting local businesses, aiming to clarify the factors that may influence operations.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has published a document outlining anticipated reasons for restrictions that may affect local businesses. The document aims to clarify the factors influencing business operations within the borough.

The council's communication highlights specific areas where restrictions could be applied, although no exact measures have been confirmed at this stage.

Business owners and stakeholders are encouraged to review the document to understand potential implications for their operations.

The council will provide further information as the situation develops, and businesses should check official council channels for updates.

articles.title: New Development Corporation Established for Northern Gateway
articles.excerpt: The Atom Valley Northern Gateway Mayoral Development Corporation has been set up to support local growth in Rochdale and Bury, focusing on jobs, homes, and infrastructure.
articles.content_html:
A new development corporation has been established to support the delivery of Northern Gateway sites in Rochdale and Bury. The Atom Valley Northern Gateway Mayoral Development Corporation was formed in January 2026 by Rochdale Council, Bury Council, and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA).

The corporation aims to facilitate local growth by focusing on the development of jobs, homes, and infrastructure. It is expected to play a significant role in the regeneration of the Northern Gateway sites.

Local authorities have expressed optimism that this initiative will enhance economic opportunities and improve living conditions for residents. The collaboration between the councils and GMCA is seen as a vital step towards achieving these goals.

Further details on specific projects and timelines are expected to be announced as the corporation begins its work in the coming months.

articles.title: New Contractor Appointed for Touchstones Rochdale Transformation
articles.excerpt: A new contractor has been appointed as the transformation of Touchstones Rochdale enters its next phase, according to the Rochdale Development Agency.
articles.content_html:
A new contractor has been appointed as the transformation of Touchstones Rochdale enters its next phase. The Rochdale Development Agency announced the development on 28 July 2026.

The project aims to enhance the cultural and community offerings at Touchstones, which serves as a key venue in Rochdale.

Details about the contractor and specific plans for the next phase of the transformation have not yet been disclosed.

Further updates are expected as the project progresses.
